Android blocks this switch for apps installed outside an app store. Allow the ^1 app-op to turn on the accessibility service. The accessibility list shows this as "Controlled by Restricted Setting".

Open App info and select "Allow restricted settings" from the menu, or run this on a computer:

^2

Either option works. The switch will work afterwards.

Automatic pairing reads the code out of the system dialog through Shizuku's accessibility service, so it has to be enabled, and only for as long as it takes: the service turns itself off once the code is found, or after a minute to save power. Shizuku normally enables it on its own, and that needs the WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission, which a fresh install has not been granted yet.

Enable it on the next screen, type the code yourself under Manual, or grant the permission once:

adb shell pm grant moe.shizuku.privileged.api android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

The system requires the pairing dialog to always be visible. Using split-screen mode is the only way to let this app and the system dialog be visible at the same time.

Samsung keeps these in the battery service data, and prints them in the battery dump. They are not part of the Android API, so another make will not have them.

Counters kept by the platform itself. They reset every time the battery is charged to full, which is why a phone charged an hour ago reads seconds here and one that has been off the charger all day reads hours.
Attributed by component, which is what this platform prints. It keeps per-app figures as wake locks and running times instead of as milliamp hours, so no per-app numbers are invented here.

The platform does not report the design capacity, and this device denies the fuel gauge even to the shell, so no percentage of a full battery can be calculated honestly. What the system has learned is above.

Every thermal sensor the kernel exposes, hottest first. A sensor with nothing attached reports the -273 sentinel and is left out, as are the power-supply trip levels, which are not temperatures. %d zones were listed.

The kernel accounting over the window named in its dump. Load is the one, five and fifteen minute average; each row is the processor time that process used, and kernel workers appear because they do the work, not only apps.

Turn it on yourself under Developer options > Wireless debugging, or grant the permission with adb shell pm grant moe.shizuku.privileged.api android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS. Once Shizuku is running it keeps that permission itself, so this is a one-off.

This device does not ship the Samsung FOTA agent (com.sdet.fotaagent), which is the only component the system start method can use, so there is nothing to escalate with here. Switch the system start method to Custom command: the app will show you what to run with an escalation your device does have.

The service did not appear within a minute. Both halves keep a log: the starter under ShizukuServiceStarter and the hand-over under BinderSender. A logcat reader filtered to those two shows whether the starter got as far as forking the server, and whether the server ever asked for the binder.
Escalate however you can, your own exploit, an automation or a root shell, and run this command: it launches the service as the system uid. The app is waiting for it to appear.

That is the half of adb that runs on a computer, and it has nothing to act on from inside the device. Run the device command itself here instead: adb shell ps and ps are the same thing.
